title: The Midnight Piercer
subtitle: Wooo-wooo! Join us in our waltz along the banks of the Danube!

trails.title: Innocence Sealed Away
trails.description: Sweet, warm dreams of yesterday, forever lost.

content.text:
Outside, it's as dark as if someone had spilled a whole bottle of ink. The glass window reflects me and little William sitting opposite each other. I bet he's not really asleep! The kerosene lamp on the table casts our shadows on the wall. I stare at them, hold my breath, and clutch my teddy bear tight.

The train clatters along the rails, like someone's chasing after us, chasing us away from Istanbul, away from Uncle's house. When Ms. Dorothy was packing our clothes, her hands were shaking so much she couldn't even fasten the buttons on my shirt. Her face was pale as paper, lips pressed tight, as if the moment she opened her mouth, all the awful words trapped in her throat would come flying out like crows. She just said, "Children, hurry! Come with me." Everything happened too fast. I didn't even have time to pack all my dolls—Jenny, Jack, Nina ... I'm sorry, I couldn't bring you with me!

Where is this train taking us? Budapest ... Father's home. Will there be a warm fireplace there? Sweet Dobos cake? The smell of roses? I've already forgotten what Father looks like ... but he must be tall ... tall enough to protect us! Like the heroes in bedtime stories ... the powerful, brave, amazing vampires who only appear at night and vanquish everything in their path!

If only ... if only a vampire would really come! They'd drain the blood of all the bad people and protect good children who behave. So they'd surely scare away whatever's hiding in the dark, whatever it is that makes Ms. Dorothy's face go pale.

I keep praying silently, again and again. I believe the great vampire will come to save us!

items.text: With a sharp whistle, the train surges forward, chugging with growing speed into the black expanse.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Phew. The train is finally moving!
Hearts long held in suspense settle, lulled by the rhythmic sway of the train.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Now, what to do when I get to Budapest? First, eat a lot of Kapama!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: No, no, wait. First thing's first. Find a job, then Kapama!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Find a job so I can eat Kapama. Eat Kapama so I can work harder.
The girl draws her kaval flute, fingers brushing the tiny cracks.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Мама, will the Kapama in Budapest taste as good as yours?
She looks out at the rolling mountains in the distance, seeing a lone figure running along their spine.
The figure dashes through a graveyard, over cold fields, beneath a sagging sky.
Her silent film is suddenly pierced with sound—a scream that only she can hear.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Whatever happens, I'll do my best to stay alive. I promise, Мама.
The girl sniffles, putting the flute away before taking a quick look around the carriage.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Ms. Semmelweis won't be back for a while, right?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: I'm here to investigate this "duplicity."

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: One last question. How familiar are you with vampiric legends?

items.speaker: Semmelweis
items.text: Vampires aren't the only dangerous things that may lurk on this train.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: She did pay for my beef stew and lark cake, but she seems really obsessed with vampires.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: No, the sooner I leave, the better.
She jumps from her seat, hesitates, then drops two coins on the table.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Forgive me, Ms. Semmelweis. I'll repay you, someday! Cross my heart!
Resolute, she turns back, searching for another refuge.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Ouch!

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: *sob*

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: I-I'm lost. *hiccup* I can't find my friends.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Uh, I'm sure you'll find them sooner or later! It's not like they were thrown off the train or something.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: So, just keep on searching! Go on, you can do it!
The girl hurries to leave, but her hem is caught.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Please help me. *sniffle* I don't know where I am.
Her sobbing echoes so loudly that people three carriages away prick their ears.
At last, she plays her trump card, removing her hat to reveal her fangs and crimson eyes.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: S-Stop crying. I'm a vampire. If you don't stop, I'll bite you!

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Really?
No fear. No disgust.
Only curiosity. Innocent wonder.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Uh, aren't you afraid of me? I'm a red-eyed vampire. See?
She leans closer, pulling down her eyelids.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Wow! Your eyes are so pretty! Like rubies!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Rubies? Never heard that one before.
She flushes red, caught off guard by the compliment.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Rubies or-or maybe the red roses of Damascus!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Roses? I—Sure they are! Roses that never wither!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Tell me more—more of these good things about vampires.
The girl circles her while jumping up and down like an excited puppy.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: But Ms. Dorothy doesn't let us read vampire stories. She says they're, um, made-up-believe. I don't care, though. I think they're amazing, don't you?

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: So I read them myself. The pure-blooded vampires are the strongest, and they live in big, big castles! You must live in one too, right?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: S-Sure I do. Now that you mention it ...

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Maybe I can tell you all about my glorious ancestors.
Rubuska coughs lightly, claps her hands, and recounts her proud history.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Ahem. Long, long, long ... a lot of longs ago, back in the earliest times.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: A most amazing ancestor of mine gave some invaders a good beating!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Yeah, that's right. He was the famous Impaler, known as Dracula, Arnold, um, Arnold V!

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Dracula! Dracula!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: My great-grandfather Arnold lived for 155 years! Then he took a wooden stake to the heart and bled to death.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Then, how old are you? Um ...

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Name's Rubuska. I'm 14 years old.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Erhm, I'm, I mean, I'm 214 years old.
She quickly corrects herself.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Yep! I've already lived two hundred plus two times seven years.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: But I'm still young for a vampire of my lineage.
The young girl speaks with fervor, reciting the stories from memory.
Stories that rise up from the endless snowy winters: silence, a blazing hearth, her head on her mother's lap, eyes drifting shut.
Fangs soaked with blood, moonlit nights, and dark castles ... She begged her mother to tell those wondrous tales again and again.
Until her voice grew faint.
And the little girl drifted into blissful sleep.
Vampire?
Children gather as if drawn by unseen magic.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: William!
The lone bird finds companions at last.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: You're here, hahaha. This is my new friend, Rubuska. She's a vampire!

items.speaker: Child I
items.text: Wow, a real-life vampire!
Excited voices fill the air, until a boy steps from the shadows, scorn written on his face.

items.speaker: Little William
items.text: How do you know she's a vampire, huh? You don't have any proof.

items.speaker: Child II
items.text: Yeah! Does she look anything like the ones in the stories?

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: She does! Her eyes are red! Like rubies!

items.speaker: Little William
items.text: But-But when Uncle Henry was sick, his eyes went all red, and you said he was a vampire too. Remember?

items.speaker: Little William
items.text: Ms. Dorothy even scolded us for being rude.

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Don't listen to him! You're a real vampire, right, Rubuska?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: O-Of course I am!
She flusters, now determined to defend the honor of her kind.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: You want proof? Then here it is. I'll show you what a real vampire looks like.
She makes a performance of strolling under the light.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Take a look. Can you find my shadow?

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Shadow ...

items.speaker: Child II
items.text: Wait, you don't have a shadow!
Shadows accompany every child, an identical twin matching the movement of their hands in the darkness.
But Rubuska stands alone. As if the light itself goes straight through her, as though she was never bound to its law, never part of the world it illuminated.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Exactly! We vampires don't have shadows.

items.speaker: Children
items.text: Vampire! Vampire!
The children cheer louder and louder, clapping with glee.

items.speaker: Little William
items.text: Whoa! She really is a bone-and-fide vampire!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Told you so.
Her pride is short-lived. Another challenge soon follows.

items.speaker: Child I
items.text: So, you're a vampire. Then you must be brave. How about the scary conductress? Have you ever talked to her?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Conductress? Umm, I mean, more than just talk. She's actually one of my best friends.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: You think she's scary, huh? I'm telling you, she's big, but she's slow. If it weren't for me ...
The children watch with rapt attention.

items.speaker: Little William
items.text: Wow, you're like a boss! Our boss!

items.speaker: Children
items.text: Boss! Boss!
She feels almost dizzy with power.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Well, if you insist ... Alright, fine. I'll be your boss.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Looks like you're having fun, "best friend."
A rumbling voice cuts through.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Y-You heard all that?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: We heard you the moment we entered the carriage. How wonderful to see you all getting along!

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: "Big but slow," is that right?

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Haha, it's just—just a game. Hahahaha.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: Play as you like, but don't block the aisle.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Sure thing, uh, old pal. Hahaha. We'll, uh, make sure we do that.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Are these your new friends, Ms. Rubuska?
The stewardess examines the gaggle of children surrounding Rubuska.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Not just friends. They're more like, uhm, familiars!

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Right, everyone?
Rubuska sniffs, proud of her new "followers."

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: Exactly! We're the familiars of the great vam—

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: Ahem, ahem! This place is too crowded. I must have a larger castle, you hear me?
She changes the subject abruptly.

items.speaker: Rubuska
items.text: When we get there, I can tell you some more stories about "that."

items.speaker: Annabelle
items.text: That? Oh, "that"!

items.speaker: Children
items.text: New stories! New stories!
The noise fades, and the carriage returns to calm.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: How lovely it is to see Ms. Rubuska making so many new friends. I'm almost a little jealous.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: You've never had many friends; is that why?

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: I …
Aima sneaks a glance at her, hesitating.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Ah, it's about time we headed back. Ms. Semmelweis must be waiting.

items.speaker: Corvus
items.text: It is. Let's go.
Before leaving, the stewardess casts a final worried look at the mischievous passenger, remembering her shadowed smile.
And those impossibly brilliant crimson eyes.

items.speaker: Aima
items.text: Rubuska ...
